intended_object: A function on bit strings used inside a GapCVP hardness reduction. It decodes a nested-node outer cell and then takes its original-source component, so that a polynomial-time Turing machine construction can be built from it. I inferred this from the vague docstring "GapCVP reduction support", the name, and how the library uses it.
explanation: The body just composes two encoding helpers specific to this library: `sourceExplicitAffineCellOriginalSource ∘ compactPhysicalLagrangeNestedNodeOuterCell`. Nearby code shows what it is for. The lemmas right after it prove it is computable in polynomial time, and it appears as the `output` field of a reduction component. It is a step inside a proof of complexity-theoretic hardness and has no counterpart as a mathematical object in the literature. Because it is an internal device, the question of whether it is faithful does not arise.
